## Context

- **AC1 is already recorded.** The parent AC4 re-scope comment on LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D (2026-10-25T20:39) references this item and the 12 user-traffic events / 7.4 h measurement with the audit split. Re-confirm it against the fresh window.
- **AC2's edge is mechanically satisfied but stale.** The depends-on edge to LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG exists and the epic is completed, yet the residual survived it. At intake the live fix owner was recorded as LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 (predicted-warmth / `measured_cache_deficit` early abort), whose F5 LP-0MVR7IXAI002QXXD owned the fix's own post-deploy measurement. **Updated at the verdict (2026-10-30):** both are terminal (Option D live from the 2026-10-29T00:10:19Z restart; F5's post-deploy window measured under LP-0MVS03KCV005BTGE) and the residual survived them — 47 user-class `prefill_deadline` evictions in the 24 h post-deploy window. The live mechanism owner is now **LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2** (abandoned-prefill backlog); see *Relationships* below.
- **AC4's rollback note is in the description.** Re-affirm it with the fresh window's numbers.

## Scope

**In:** the AC3 verdict; the AC3(b) producer re-scope proposal when path (a) fails; evidence, link and rollback recording on this item and in a parent-AC4 comment on LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D; description updates limited to the Ownership / Relationships / Key Files lines that the measurements proved stale.

**Out:** any code change; any change to parent AC4 text or thresholds without explicit producer approval (AC3(b)); measurement work (the sibling measurement item).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Parent AC1 (Evidence recorded).** "**AC1 — Evidence recorded.** The 22-event/7.4 h measurement (12 user-traffic) with the `progress=0` signature and the audit-load split is referenced from the parent AC4 comment." — re-confirmed with the post-occupancy-fix window and referenced from a parent AC4 comment.
- **AC2 — Parent AC2 (Link established).** "**AC2 — Link established.** A related edge points to LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG so the producer can fold this into the scheduler scope (or explicitly re-scope parent AC4 to exclude audit traffic / warm-HOL)." — recorded as satisfied (depends-on edge present; epic completed 2026-10-25T23:44Z).

- **AC3 — Parent AC3 (Closure).** "**AC3 — Closure.** Closed only when either (a) the scheduler epic lands and a post-landing window shows zero user-traffic `prefill_deadline` evictions after acceptance, or (b) the producer explicitly re-scopes parent AC4 with an agreed threshold and the re-scoped criterion is met." — a written verdict records which path applies: either (a) is certified from the measurement window, or (a) fails and an AC3(b) re-scope proposal (recommended user-traffic threshold, rationale and measurement plan) is put to the producer with `wl reviewed LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I true`. No parent AC4 text, threshold or AC is changed without an explicit producer reply recorded on this item; the item closes only on the matching condition.
- **AC4 — Parent AC4 (Rollback note).** "**AC4 — Rollback note.** No rollback recommended: the budget change is working (−88 % deadline rate, 0 over-budget admissions, −83 % wasted tokens); rolling back restores the thrash without touching this residual." — re-affirmed with the fresh window's numbers and recorded on this item and in the parent AC4 comment.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/admission_events.py` (`EVICTION_REASONS`, `log_local_eviction`) — the closed reason vocabulary the verdict reports against
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` (`ProjectedWait`, `evaluate_admission`) — the admission maths the rollback note refers to
- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` — the window evidence the verdict cites
- `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` — the analyser that produces every figure the verdict cites (same classifier as the parent AC4 measurement)
- `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md` and `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual-2026-10-29.json` — the recorded report and per-event dataset (commit `56d853be`)

## Relationships (successor links, recorded 2026-10-30 — AC2b)

The residual survived the scheduler epic **and** the Option D fix, so the fix ownership is re-pointed here. Recorded as this description plus a related-to comment, deliberately **not** as a `wl dep add` edge: a dependency on a non-terminal item would set this verdict item `blocked` before its own recording work can run.

- **Superseded fix owner:** LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 (Option D `measured_cache_deficit` early abort, F4 `1908f431`) with F5 LP-0MVR7IXAI002QXXD and its post-deploy delegate LP-0MVS03KCV005BTGE — all terminal; their own ≥24 h post-deploy window still shows 47 user-class `prefill_deadline` evictions.
- **Live mechanism owner (successor):** LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2 — an early-released dispatch keeps prefilling in `llama-server` and starves the next dispatch (26 % of the day's prefill compute thrown away; 58 of the 60 measured events started inside an abandoned-prefill window). Discovered from the measurement item LP-0MVRMOT0N005136O.
- **Predecessor evidence:** LP-0MVRMOT0N005136O (measured window, `completed` — this item's blocker, satisfied).
- **Parent-AC4 owner:** LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D — its AC4 carries the residual clause; the refreshed evidence comment was posted there with this verdict.
- **Superseded hypothesis, stated explicitly:** second-slot head-of-line blocking (a warm prompt blocked behind another session's prefill) is **superseded** — it explains 9 of 60 events (15 %), and none of those 9 had another session's lease extended inside its window. The dominant cause (43 of 60, 72 %) is predicted-but-unmeasured warmth: priced at ~95 % cached (`p50` priced cached ratio 0.946), zero backend prefill progress for the whole 120 s lease, and a retry that re-enters at the same price — kept alive by the abandoned-prefill backlog.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — producer availability.** AC3(b) needs an explicit producer reply; if none arrives the item stays open with the question recorded (AC3).
- **Risk — stale-link confusion.** Recording the successor link as a `wl dep add` edge would set this item `blocked`; the description/comment form in AC2b preserves dispatchability at the cost of a softer link.
- **Risk — re-scope fatigue.** The parent AC4 has already been re-scoped once (2026-10-25); the AC3(b) proposal must state why a further re-scope is warranted rather than assuming it.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the sibling measurement item. The closure certification also needs LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 (fix) and its F5 LP-0MVR7IXAI002QXXD (post-deploy measurement) to be terminal; this is recorded as a stated prerequisite rather than a `wl dep add` edge so the recording work remains dispatchable.

## Deliverables

A verdict comment on this item (path (a) certified, or (a)-fails plus the AC3(b) proposal), the parent-AC4 evidence comment on LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D, and the re-affirmed rollback note.

## Goal

As an operator I need a **measured, reproducible verdict** on whether
`/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics` (the `amd_gpu_metrics_v3_0` blob, the
interface `amdgpu_top` reads) carries a *graded* GFX-activity signal on this
Strix Halo APU — one that separates compute from idle the way the
power-derived `gpu:computing:bool` rule does but `gpu_busy_percent` does not —
and, only if such a field passes an explicit discrimination bar, to have it
published as a Prometheus series through the existing 10 s textfile sampler.
A negative verdict, recorded with numbers so the path is never retried, is an
equally valid outcome.

## Problem statement

The usage report's GPU busy time infers activity from power draw
(`gpu:computing:bool >= bool 90`), which cannot tell GFX work from any other
power draw. `gpu_busy_percent` was eliminated as a utilisation signal
(2026-10-28: 45.2 % false-busy, Pearson r = 0.28 against power,
LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL), leaving `gpu_metrics` as the last candidate hardware
activity source. **Intake measurements (2026-10-29) show that candidate is very
probably dead too**: `average_gfx_activity` read **100 % on every one of 120
samples across two captures** while package power moved between 42 W and 123 W
and DRAM bandwidth between 0.7 and 59.5 GB/s. This item therefore exists to
settle the question with evidence and a stated bar, not to assume the answer.

## Users

- **Operator (primary).** "Is the GPU actually doing work right now, and was it
  busy between 17:00 and 19:00?" — needs a utilisation figure that is a direct
  measurement, not a power-draw proxy.
- **Agent answering a usage/incident question (secondary).** Needs to know which
  hardware fields are trustworthy on this host so it cites a real signal instead
  of re-litigating `gpu_busy_percent`.

User stories:

- As an operator I can run one command that decodes `gpu_metrics`, samples it
  alongside power and `gpu_busy_percent`, and prints per-field discrimination
  statistics — so the verdict rests on numbers I can reproduce.
- As an operator I am told plainly whether the interface gives a graded signal,
  with the capture date, kernel, sample counts and band means, so I never
  re-investigate it.
- As an operator, if a field does pass, the series appears next to the existing
  `gpu_*` textfile series without a new daemon, port or scrape job.

## Existing state (measured during intake, 2026-10-29, kernel 7.0.0-34-generic)

| Question | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Is the file live and readable? | `-r--r--r-- 4096` root:root; 264 bytes of content; values change between reads; no root, no ROCm, no `amd-smi` needed |
| Which structure? | Header decodes to `structure_size=264, format_revision=3, content_revision=0` → `struct gpu_metrics_v3_0` (`drivers/gpu/drm/amd/include/kgd_pp_interface.h`; the same header text is vendored in `libdrm_amdgpu_sys`'s `wrapper_gpu_metrics.h`) |
| Does the layout check out? | Field sizes under `#pragma pack(4)` sum to 260 B; 4 B tail padding = **264 B**, matching `structure_size` exactly. Cross-checks: `average_socket_power` 95 060 mW vs hwmon `power1_average` 95.06 W (0.1 % agreement); `average_gfx_power` 11.3–44.2 W; `average_gfxclk_frequency` 2 711–2 900 MHz; `average_dram_reads` 0.7–59.5 GB/s; `average_vcn_activity` 0; `average_ipu_activity` all 0; `temperature_gfx` 56–69 °C |
| Does the activity field discriminate? | **No.** Capture A (60 samples @1 s): power 44–123 W, DRAM 1.8–59.5 GB/s → `average_gfx_activity` = 100 on all 60. Capture B (60 samples @1 s): power 42–66 W (idle band), DRAM 0.7–3.5 GB/s → 100 on all 60. Spot samples earlier: 97, 99, 100 at 41–57 W |
| How does it compare with the rejected counter? | Identically saturated: `gpu_busy_percent` = 100 on all 120 samples of both captures; `rocm-smi --showuse` reports `GPU use 100 %` at 54 W. GFX clock is pinned at its 2 900 MHz maximum in *both* bands, so the GFX domain is never gated while the proxy holds the device |
| What *does* vary with load? | `average_dram_reads`/`average_dram_writes` (memory bandwidth, 0.7 → 59.5 GB/s), `average_gfx_power` (11.3 → 44.2 W), `average_socket_power` (42 → 123 W), `average_core_c0_activity` (per-core C0 residency) |
| Are the values instantaneous? | No — they are SMU **time filtered** (`time_filter_alphavalue` = 1 000 000); the filter window is undocumented, so no claim finer than the sample interval is supportable |

Existing pipeline this would plug into: `gpu-metrics.service` runs
`~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` every 10 s, writing `gpu.prom` into
node_exporter's textfile collector (`gpu_busy_percent`, `gpu_vram_*`,
`gpu_gtt_used_bytes`, label `gpu="card0"`), scraped every 15 s by Prometheus;
documented in [docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service](../../docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service)
and [monitoring/README.md](../../monitoring/README.md).

## Desired change

1. **A reproducible probe CLI** — `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py`: decode the
   v3.0 blob from a sysfs path (default
   `/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics`), sample every candidate activity
   field alongside the two reference signals (amdgpu hwmon `power1_average` and
   `gpu_busy_percent`) at a configurable interval for a configurable duration,
   and emit CSV or `--json`. A `--verdict` mode prints the per-field
   discrimination statistics against the bar below.
2. **A recorded verdict** — the measured numbers plus a pass/fail decision per
   candidate field, written into the work item and the two monitoring documents,
   so the interface is either adopted once or closed off permanently.
3. **Conditional publication** — only if a field passes the bar, publish it
   through the existing 10 s textfile sampler (new `# HELP`/`# TYPE` series with
   the `gpu="card0"` label, atomic write, nothing written on read failure). If
   nothing passes, publish nothing and record why.
4. **A regression guard** — a saturated activity field must not be usable as a
   utilisation input in any rule or report query without a test failing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py` decodes `gpu_metrics` into named fields
  using the pinned v3.0 layout and validates the header
  (`structure_size` == layout size, `format_revision` == 3); unit tests cover a
  real 264-byte capture committed as a fixture, a truncated buffer, and an
  unknown `format_revision`/`structure_size`, which must be rejected with a
  clear error rather than misparsed.
- [ ] A capture (`--duration`/`--interval`, defaults documented) writes one row
  per sample containing a timestamp, every candidate activity field,
  `power1_average_watts` and `gpu_busy_percent`; a test drives the sampler
  against fixture sysfs trees (fake `/sys/class/drm/card0/device` and hwmon
  directory) and asserts row count, monotonic timestamps and fixture-derived
  values, without sleeping.
- [ ] `--verdict` reports, per candidate field, the idle-band mean (< 60 W), the
  compute-band mean (≥ 90 W), their separation in percentage points, Pearson r
  against package power, and the idle-band false-busy share (samples ≥ 90 %
  while power < 60 W); a field passes only if separation ≥ 30 pp **and**
  r ≥ 0.6 **and** idle-band false-busy ≤ 10 %. Unit tests drive synthetic
  saturated, graded and noisy series and assert the exact pass/fail decision and
  the printed statistics.
- [ ] The measured numbers and the resulting verdict — positive **or** negative
  — are recorded in `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`,
  `monitoring/README.md` (the "Why not `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi` or `amdtop`?"
  section gains a `gpu_metrics` row) and the work item, including capture date,
  kernel version, sample counts and band statistics; a negative verdict is a
  complete outcome, not a failure.
- [ ] If a field passed, the 10 s textfile sampler publishes it (series name,
  `# HELP`/`# TYPE`, `gpu="card0"` label) with the existing atomic-write and
  write-nothing-on-failure behaviour, and `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`
  documents the series and its meaning; a test runs the sampler against fixture
  sysfs and asserts its emitted series set exactly matches the set the
  documentation table lists (so docs and behaviour cannot drift). If no field
  passed, no new series is added and the test asserts the sampler's series set is
  unchanged.
- [ ] The pinned-counter guard in `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py`
  (`FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES`) is extended so a saturated activity field cannot
  appear as a utilisation input — `gpu_busy_percent` always, and the
  `gpu_metrics` activity fields when the verdict is negative — with a regression
  test that fails if any `monitoring/*.yaml` rule expression or the probe's own
  utilisation expressions select one.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, docstrings, `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` and
  `monitoring/README.md`; the probe's re-measure procedure (how to re-run the
  capture after a kernel, firmware or driver change) is documented.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes via `/skill:test`.

## Constraints

- **No new daemon, port or scrape job.** Reuse `gpu-metrics.service` →
  node_exporter textfile collector; the sampler's 10 s cadence and Prometheus's
  15 s scrape interval are the resolution floor and must be stated as such.
- **Host state is part of the deliverable.** The sampler script lives in
  `~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` and is documented in
  `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`; any change to its series must be reflected
  there so a clean clone can reproduce it.
- **Repository boundary.** `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` (`gpu_busy.py`,
  `reporting.py`) is not edited — adopting a passing field in the daily report is
  a follow-up item, mirroring the constraint recorded in LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W.
- **The layout must be pinned in-repo.** The struct is not shipped in the
  installed `linux-headers` packages on this host, so the field table must be
  transcribed with a cited source (`struct gpu_metrics_v3_0`) and validated
  against the observed 264-byte `structure_size`; it must fail closed when the
  kernel reports a different revision.
- **No instantaneous claims.** The values are SMU time-filtered with an
  undocumented window; the output must say so rather than imply per-second
  fidelity.
- **Read cost.** One 264-byte sysfs read per sample; world-readable, no root, no
  ROCm userspace, no `amd-smi`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py` — New. v3.0 decoder (field table + header
  validation), paired sampler for `gpu_metrics` + hwmon power + `gpu_busy_percent`,
  band statistics and the pass/fail verdict; CSV and `--json` output.
- `tests/test_gpu_metrics_probe.py` — New. Decoder fixtures (real 264-byte
  capture, truncated, unknown revision), fixture-sysfs sampling, verdict
  arithmetic and boundary cases (power exactly 60 W / 90 W, activity exactly
  90 %).
- `tests/fixtures/gpu_metrics_v3_0.bin` — New. One committed real capture so the
  layout assertion is reproducible.
- `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` — Record the verdict, the decode layout and
  (conditionally) the new series; extend the verification section with the probe
  command.
- `monitoring/README.md` — Add `gpu_metrics` to "Why not `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi`
  or `amdtop`?" with the measured band statistics; note the re-measure recipe.
- `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml` — Header comment records the `gpu_metrics`
  verdict (no rule change expected; the power rule stays authoritative).
- `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` — Extend `FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES`
  so saturated activity fields are rejected as utilisation inputs.
- `~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` — Only if a field passed: emit the new
  series from the same atomic write.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: the premise is false.** Intake evidence already shows
  `average_gfx_activity` saturated at 100 % from 42 W to 123 W. Mitigation: the
  negative verdict is an explicit, accepted outcome (AC4) and the probe records
  which fields *do* discriminate (DRAM bandwidth, GFX power) for a follow-up.
- **Risk: decoder drift after a kernel or firmware upgrade.** Mitigation: header
  validation plus a committed real capture; the probe refuses unknown revisions
  and the docs carry the re-measure procedure.
- **Risk: undocumented APU field semantics.** `average_gfx_activity` may mean
  "GFX domain powered" rather than "GFX busy" on SMU 14. Mitigation: the bar and
  band statistics decide it, and the interpretation limits are documented.
- **Risk: a capture that misses one band.** A verdict computed only from idle
  samples would be meaningless. Mitigation: AC3 requires both bands, and the
  probe reports per-band sample counts so a one-sided capture is visible.
- **Risk: scope creep** into report integration, new daemons or a full GPU
  telemetry redesign. Mitigation: those are explicit constraints/follow-ups, not
  scope.
- **Assumption:** amdgpu hwmon `power1_average` remains the reference compute
  signal (idle ≈ 40–54 W, computing ≈ 115 W, threshold 90 W) per
  LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48; this item does not re-derive the threshold.
- **Assumption:** the discrimination bar (≥ 30 pp separation, r ≥ 0.6, ≤ 10 %
  idle false-busy) is strict enough — it is far stricter than
  `gpu_busy_percent`'s measured 45.2 % false-busy — and is recorded here so the
  producer can tighten or relax it before implementation.
- **Assumption:** both bands occur on this host within a short window (intake saw
  idle at 42–66 W and compute at 90–123 W within ~15 minutes), so a 30-minute
  capture is sufficient; longer captures are supported by the same CLI.
- **Assumption:** priority stays `high` — the verdict decides whether a direct
  hardware utilisation measure is possible at all on this host, which the usage
  report's honesty goal depends on — even though the likely outcome is a short
  negative report rather than a code change.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL** — Evaluate `amd-smi` as the GPU utilisation source
  (completed). Quantified `gpu_busy_percent`'s saturation (45.2 % false-busy,
  r = 0.28) and filed this item as the remaining avenue. Parent context.
- **LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W** — Add GPU telemetry sampler for true utilisation
  history (in review). Owns the *workload* half (per-slot busy/idle, in-flight
  tasks, the `gpu_utilisation.py` CLI). **Partial overlap only**: that item
  attributes power to llama-server slots; this one judges a *hardware* activity
  field. No CLI or slot work is duplicated here — this item produces a probe and
  a verdict, and its publication step (if any) extends the existing sysfs
  sampler.
- **LP-0MVO8CLCL00086NT** — Monitoring: deployable, tailnet-exposed Prometheus
  with honest GPU utilisation (completed) and children: LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48
  (power-derived utilisation rules), LP-0MVO8DORX004P05G (docs for the deployed
  stack). The sampler, units and docs this item extends.
- **LP-0MS9GA6QL007XTBP** — Fix GPU-wedge false positives (completed):
  established that `gpu_busy_percent` is unusable and power is the
  discriminating signal; the proxy's wedge detector was disabled because of it.
- **LP-0MVOHRLPB0086Q5T** — Grafana dashboard GPU VRAM panel queries series no
  exporter publishes (in progress): the precedent for asserting *published*
  series against documentation, which AC5 reuses.
- **LP-0MVNWULLI006ZYXX** — Cross-check report slot-time against llama-server
  eval timings (independent): the other half of validating the report's busy
  figures.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive operator was available for this intake (auto-dispatched by the
herdr downtime worker at 2026-10-29T03:54:28Z), so each question below was
resolved from host and repository evidence; none is blocking. Each carries the
agent's **Recommended** option, which the producer may override.

- **Q1: Given that `average_gfx_activity` already measures as saturated (100 %
  from 42 W to 123 W), is a documented negative verdict an acceptable
  deliverable for this item?**
  **Recommended:** yes — record the numbers, close the path permanently, and file
  follow-ups for the fields that do discriminate.
  — Answer (research, 2026-10-29): the item was written to test the hypothesis,
  not to assume it; the file decodes correctly (264 B v3.0, cross-checked
  against hwmon power) yet its activity field does not respond to load, so the
  honest outcome is a negative verdict with evidence. Source: two 60-sample 1 s
  captures (power 44–123 W and 42–66 W, DRAM 0.7–59.5 GB/s, activity 100 on all
  120 samples), `/tmp` probe using the `kgd_pp_interface.h` v3.0 layout.
- **Q2: If a field does pass the bar, should it replace the power-derived
  `gpu:computing:bool` as the report's GPU busy measure, or be published
  alongside it?**
  **Recommended:** publish alongside; keep power-derived authoritative until its
  own calibration item justifies switching.
  — Answer (research, 2026-10-29): `gpu:computing:bool` is referenced by the
  report (`gpu_busy.py`, `reporting.py`), the alert `GpuComputingSustained` and
  `monitoring/tests/gpu_rules_test.yml`; changing its meaning inside an
  investigation item would break three consumers at once. Publishing an additive
  series keeps the comparison visible, and report adoption stays a follow-up
  (same boundary recorded in LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W). Source:
  `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml`, `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/gpu_busy.py`.
- **Q3: Where should the probe live, and how should a passing field reach
  Prometheus — extend the deployed bash textfile sampler, or add a Python
  sampler?**
  **Recommended:** a repo `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py` decoder plus a one-line
  call from the existing bash sampler; no new unit.
  — Answer (research, 2026-10-29): the sampler is a documented 10 s bash loop
  writing `gpu.prom` atomically, and `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` embeds
  the script verbatim; a second sampler would duplicate the unit, the textfile
  directory and the docs. Decoding a 264-byte binary blob in bash is not
  testable, so the field table belongs in Python with fixture tests. Source:
  `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`, `~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh`.

# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the post-flip window measured against the ≥24 h pre-flip
baseline and a keep/rollback verdict recorded, so the sweep is judged by its
own flip criteria instead of by assumption.

Part of LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R. Delivers the evaluation half of parent AC1
(trigger, observation window, verdict) and AC3's "run the report and record the
numbers".

## Nature of the task

This is a **scheduled measurement task, not code work**. It starts only after
the sweep child has shipped to `dev`, been released, and the proxy has been
restarted in a quiet window. It is expected to stay open for the 7-day
observation window; it must not be implemented inside a code session.

## Acceptance criteria

# Slot-cache cleanup: protect recent orphan sidecars from the orphan sweep

## Problem statement

`scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh` rule 3 (orphan sidecars, added by commit
`5502ee44` under LP-0MVK0E80C009HUQC) deletes **every** `.ratio.json` sidecar
whose `slot_<session>.bin` snapshot is gone, with no age guard. Every other
deletion rule in the script protects a recent artefact (`--min-age-days`, the
size rule's protective window), so the orphan rule is the one path that can
delete a file written moments ago — for example a sidecar whose snapshot is
momentarily absent while a save/restore is settling, or a save that failed
between writing the sidecar and the snapshot. The original acceptance criteria
for LP-0MVK0E80C009HUQC required "a sidecar whose snapshot is missing and which
is older than `--min-age-days` is deleted; a recent orphan is kept"; only the
first half shipped.

## Users

**Operator (primary).** Wants orphan pruning to be aggressive on genuinely
stale files while never racing a live save: "When I raise `--min-age-days` to
protect active sessions, I expect that protection to cover sidecars too, not
just snapshots."

**Maintainer (secondary).** Wants the script's three deletion rules to share
one mental model: age-bounded, never deleting anything inside the protective
window.

Example user stories:

- As an operator, I want a just-written orphan sidecar to survive one cleanup
  cycle, so a transient missing snapshot does not destroy the routing ratio
  that the next save is about to re-pair.
- As a maintainer, I want `--min-age-days 0` to disable the protection for a
  one-off aggressive sweep, consistent with the size rule.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (guard).** An orphan sidecar whose mtime is **older** than
  `--min-age-days` is deleted; an orphan sidecar **newer** than
  `--min-age-days` is kept and reported as kept. Proven by a test in both
  suites (see AC5).
- **AC2 (dry-run).** `--dry-run` reports both categories (deletable orphan and
  kept-recent orphan) and deletes nothing; exit code stays `0`.
- **AC3 (no regression of `5502ee44`).** Endpoint-subdirectory scanning,
  snapshot+sidecar pair deletion, root-layout support, and orphan pruning for
  aged orphans all stay green. The existing pytest pin
  `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py::TestCleanupScriptRetention::test_orphan_sidecars_are_pruned_with_no_snapshots_present`
  writes orphans with mtime "now" and asserts they are deleted — it must be
  updated to age those orphans beyond `--min-age-days` (so it keeps testing
  the same rule rather than being weakened), not deleted or skipped.
- **AC4 (output & exit codes).** Existing output lines, summary lines and exit
  codes are unchanged; any new "kept" reporting is additive (only printed when
  the count is non-zero) and still reports `SUMMARY`/`DRY-RUN SUMMARY`. The
  script exits `0` when the cache contains only recent orphans.
- **AC5 (testing).** Behaviour is asserted by executable tests that run in the
  project suite: extend
  `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py::TestCleanupScriptRetention`
  (pytest-collected, the authoritative pin) **and** the standalone shell
  harness `tests/test_cleanup_slot_cache.sh` (parity for manual runs).
- **AC6 (docs).** Documentation is updated: the script header's rule-3 comment
  (`scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh`), the "Retention and pairing" paragraph in
  `proxy/docs/routing.md`, and the "Slot Cache Retention" section in
  `proxy/README.md` all state that the orphan sweep honours `--min-age-days`.
- **AC7 (suite).** The full project test suite passes with the change,
  including `proxy/tests/test_slot_pool_sizing_doc.py`'s line-number citations
  of `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh:27-28`.

## Constraints

- **Scope is one rule.** Do not re-ship or re-litigate `5502ee44`; no changes
  to recursion, pair deletion, `--dry-run` structure, arg parsing or the
  writer side (`proxy/proxy/session.py`, `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py`).
- **Keep the age semantics identical to the size rule:** protection applies
  when `age_seconds < min_age_seconds` (`--min-age-days 0` ⇒ no protection).
  Compare the **sidecar's own mtime** — the snapshot is gone, so there is no
  other timestamp available.
- **Citation-drift budget.** `proxy/tests/test_slot_pool_sizing_doc.py` pins
  `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh` lines 27 (`MAX_AGE_DAYS=7`) and 28
  (`MAX_SIZE_GB=20`) with `CITATION_DRIFT_TOLERANCE = 60`. The guard belongs in
  the orphan loop near the end of the file, so do not shift those two
  assignments by more than ~60 lines (i.e. no large new preamble). See
  LP-0MVTHK9090067ESU for the durable fix to this fragile guard — do not
  attempt that fix here.
- **Defaults stay as they are:** `MIN_AGE_DAYS=1` (1 day). The
  `proxy/benchmarks/slot_snapshot_band_report.py` parser
  (`^\s*MIN_AGE_DAYS=(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*$`) and
  `proxy/tests/test_slot_snapshot_band_report.py` assert exact default values,
  so the assignment must remain a plain `MIN_AGE_DAYS=<n>` line.
- **UK English** in all code comments and docs.

## Existing state

- `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh` — rule 1 (age), rule 2 (size, min-age
  protected), rule 3 (orphan sidecars, **unprotected**). `MIN_AGE_DAYS=1` is
  parsed and already used only by rule 2. `all_sidecars` is collected over the
  cache root plus one level of `{host}-{port}/` subdirectories.
- `tests/test_cleanup_slot_cache.sh` — 9 shell tests, 7 assertions from
  `5502ee44`; `test_orphan_sidecars_pruned` writes orphans with "now" mtime and
  asserts they are pruned.
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py::TestCleanupScriptRetention` —
  5 pytest tests invoking the script via `subprocess`; the orphan test has the
  same "now"-mtime assumption and is the pin that will go red if AC3 is missed.
- Docs: `proxy/docs/routing.md` ("Retention and pairing in
  `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh`", plus the orphan-count `find` recipe at
  ~line 757), `proxy/README.md` §"Slot Cache Retention".
- Related rationale: the sidecar TTL is `session_slot_ratio_ttl_seconds`
  (default 86 400 s = 1 day, `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py:68`), so an
  orphan younger than the default `--min-age-days` is still inside the window
  where it could legitimately be re-paired; an older one can never be credited.

## Desired change

1. In the rule-3 loop, compute the sidecar's age from `stat -c %Y`; if
   `age_seconds < min_age_seconds`, skip it and count/report it as kept
   (in `--dry-run` and in real runs alike). Keep the existing
   `[[ -f "$snapshot" ]] && continue` guard first, and preserve the
   `rm -f`/`WARNING` error path and the `errors` counter.
2. Add an additive summary line (e.g. `SUMMARY: N orphan sidecar(s) kept (newer
   than --min-age-days)`) printed only when `N > 0`, in both the real and
   `--dry-run` summary blocks.
3. Extend the pytest pin `TestCleanupScriptRetention` with: stale orphan
   deleted, recent orphan kept, `--dry-run` reporting both and deleting
   neither; fix the existing orphan test's mtime assumption.
4. Extend `tests/test_cleanup_slot_cache.sh` with the same three assertions.
5. Update the three doc locations named in AC6.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh` — rule-3 loop (age guard + kept counter),
  summary blocks, header comment for rule 3. Nothing above line 27 changes.
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py` — `TestCleanupScriptRetention`:
  add orphan age-guard tests; age the orphans in the existing pruning test
  (`_run` already forwards `*extra`, so `--min-age-days` is easy to pass).
- `tests/test_cleanup_slot_cache.sh` — `test_orphan_sidecars_pruned` plus new
  cases; needs a `make_orphan`-style helper that sets the sidecar mtime.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — "#### Retention and pairing in
  `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh`" paragraph.
- `proxy/README.md` — §"Slot Cache Retention" default-policy bullets and usage
  examples.

## Verification commands (copy-paste ready)

```bash
# Behaviour by hand (stale orphan deleted, recent orphan kept)
tmp=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$tmp/cache/localhost-8080"
echo '{}' > "$tmp/cache/slot_stale.bin.ratio.json"
touch -d "3 days ago" "$tmp/cache/slot_stale.bin.ratio.json"
echo '{}' > "$tmp/cache/localhost-8080/slot_fresh.bin.ratio.json"
./scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh --path "$tmp/cache" --dry-run   # both categories, deletes nothing
./scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh --path "$tmp/cache"             # stale gone, fresh kept

# Suite-visible pin
/skill:test --scope changed        # exercises TestCleanupScriptRetention

# Standalone shell harness (manual parity)
bash tests/test_cleanup_slot_cache.sh
```

## Related work

- **LP-0MVK0E80C009HUQC** (completed, commit `5502ee44`) — shipped recursion,
  pair deletion and orphan pruning; this item is its residual AC.
- **LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3** (completed) — the diagnosis that measured 139
  orphans / 0 snapshots and 24.2 % `missing_snapshot` seed decisions; this item
  was discovered from it.
- **LP-0MVTJVNSO008IZEB** (open) — the ≥24 h re-measurement of the seed fix;
  its `missing_snapshot` counter now decays over `--min-age-days` instead of
  instantly (see Risks).
- **LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E** (open) — writer-side sidecar/snapshot coupling and
  the restored-prefix warmness gap; adjacent but out of scope.
- **LP-0MVTHK9090067ESU** (open) — durable fix for the pool-sizing doc
  citation-drift failures; constrains AC7 here but is not addressed here.
- **LP-0MS91DHQE006CJC4** (completed) — the original "slot-cache GC
  ineffective / 97 GB" episode that established the age+size retention rules.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: the guard could mask a real orphan leak.** Recent orphans stay on
  disk for up to `--min-age-days`, so `slot_ratio_seed outcome=missing_snapshot`
  counts decay over that window instead of dropping immediately. Mitigation:
  the kept-orphan summary line keeps the residual visible; LP-0MVTJVNSO008IZEB
  should read the count after the window, not the day of deploy.
- **Risk: an existing test goes red silently.** The pytest orphan pin asserts
  deletion of "now"-aged orphans; AC3 makes fixing it explicit. Mitigation:
  update it in the same commit, never `skip`.
- **Risk: citation drift.** Covered by the constraint above (guard lives near
  the end of the file; <60 lines of preamble change).
- **Risk: scope creep** — the `proxy/README.md` section also documents a
  non-existent `--keep-recent 3` flag (stale since before `5502ee44`). Do
  **not** fix that here; it is a separate documentation defect (candidate
  follow-up item, not filed by this intake).
- **Assumption:** "kept" reporting is additive and conditional (`> 0`), so
  existing log-scraping and the `DRY-RUN SUMMARY` format keep working.
- **Assumption:** the protective comparison is the same `<` used by the size
  rule, so `--min-age-days 0` disables the guard.
- **Assumption:** no writer-side change is needed — `_retire_session_slot_snapshots()`
  already deletes snapshot and sidecar together, so the guard only narrows the
  cleanup script's blast radius.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Does the orphan sweep need the age guard at all, given the writer now
  retires pairs atomically?**
  Answer (Map, 2026-10-30, from repo evidence): Yes. The writer path
  (`proxy/proxy/session.py::_retire_session_slot_snapshots`) is atomic for
  *retirement*, but a save that fails or is in flight can still leave a
  sidecar without its snapshot, and the original LP-0MVK0E80C009HUQC AC
  explicitly required the recent-orphan case. Research: read
  `_retire_slot_snapshot` / `_retire_session_slot_snapshots`; no temp-file +
  rename in the save path, so a transient absence is possible. Source: repo
  inspection.
- **Q: Which mtime defines an orphan's age — the sidecar's or the (missing)
  snapshot's?**
  Answer (Map): the sidecar's own mtime; the snapshot does not exist, and the
  sidecar is written after the snapshot, so its mtime is the conservative
  (later) timestamp. Source: `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh` rule 3 +
  `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py` write path.
- **Q: Is `tests/test_cleanup_slot_cache.sh` executed by the project suite?**
  Answer (Map): No — the full suite is `pytest` (`.pi/test-config.json` adds no
  `suiteCommands`; the runner resolves `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings`),
  and `.sh` files are not collected. The suite-visible pin for this script is
  `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py::TestCleanupScriptRetention`.
  Both are extended (AC5) so manual shell runs keep parity. Source: test runner
  resolution + repo grep for wrappers.
- **Q: Should the default `--min-age-days` change?**
  Answer (Map): No. It stays `MIN_AGE_DAYS=1`, which also matches the sidecar
  TTL default (86 400 s), so the protection window coincides with the period in
  which an orphan could still be re-paired and credited. Changing the default
  would also break `proxy/tests/test_slot_snapshot_band_report.py` and the
  operator-facing retention docs. Source: `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py:68`,
  `proxy/benchmarks/slot_snapshot_band_report.py`.
- **OPEN QUESTION (deferred, non-blocking):** whether the stale `--keep-recent`
  flag documented in `proxy/README.md` should be corrected in this item. Not
  included in scope; recorded as a candidate follow-up.

## Related work (automated report)

> `/skill:find-related` output, recorded for auditability. Relevance is
> keyword-driven and low here — the curated **Related work** section above is
> authoritative. Full unmatched output:
> `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-LP-0MVTFJ04T001VW47.md`.

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7** – Instrument slot-sidecar seed outcomes at INFO (measure before fixing) (completed) — *relevant*: defines the `missing_snapshot` outcome vocabulary this rule affects.
- **LP-0MR4XEDEY009JGVC** – Implement: pi session log retention script (completed) — *not relevant*: different retention script.
- **LP-0MRAWF4SZ001MCGD** – Implement: session recording cleanup script (completed) — *not relevant*: different retention script.

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts*.txt` — matched only on generic
  prose tokens (`acceptance`, `added`, `age`, `ago`, …); a vendored dataset, not
  related to this item.

## Plan: changelog

Planned 2026-10-30 by `/skill:plan` (session `herdr-1793338106-3027803-27185`).

- Decomposed into 2 children, in test-first-then-docs order:
  - **LP-0MVUJBFRL005VDNA** — *Orphan sweep honours --min-age-days* (`bug`, medium):
    rule-3 age guard + kept reporting, pytest pin update plus three new cases,
    shell-harness parity. Covers AC1-AC5 and AC7 of this item.
  - **LP-0MVUJBJF9005SIFB** — *Document the orphan age guard* (`docs`, medium):
    script header rule-3 comment, `proxy/docs/routing.md` retention paragraph,
    `proxy/README.md` "Slot Cache Retention". Covers AC6 of this item.
- Dependency: LP-0MVUJBJF9005SIFB **depends on** LP-0MVUJBFRL005VDNA (docs must
  describe shipped behaviour).
- AC coverage review: 7/7 parent ACs covered (100 %), recommendation `proceed`.
- Duplicate check: `wl search` on "orphan sidecar", "min-age-days" and
  "cleanup-slot-cache" found no overlapping item — LP-0MVK0E80C009HUQC (the
  parent rule's implementation) is already complete and this item is its declared
  residual AC.
- Effort/risk re-estimated against the child WBS (see the latest effort_and_risk
  comment).

### Review decision: test-first without a test-only child

The skill prefers test/verification children before implementation children, but
the dev-push gate runs the **full suite** on every push, so a test-only child would
leave `dev` red and unpushable. LP-0MVUJBFRL005VDNA therefore carries tests and
implementation as one green slice, with an explicit TDD instruction inside it
(write the failing pytest cases first, then the guard, commit together).

## Appendix (plan session, 2026-10-30)

- **No new clarifying questions were required.** The intake Appendix above already
  answers the four design questions (is the guard needed given atomic pair
  retirement; which mtime defines age; whether the shell harness runs in CI;
  whether the default changes). The plan re-used those answers as evidence
  (work-item ids, file paths, commit `5502ee44`).
- **Q: One child or several?** Answer (plan, agent): two — code+tests, then docs.
  The change is one rule, but the docs slice is independently deliverable and keeps
  each implement session focused; expected effort is 5.9 h (9.2 h recommended), so
  a single child would be oversized.
- **Q: Should the parent's hard-wrapped AC bullets be reformatted?** Answer (plan):
  no. They read correctly for humans; the `tree_coverage` extractor reads only the
  first line of each bullet, so the children's ACs were worded to mirror those
  first lines instead of mutating intake-authored ACs.
- **OPEN QUESTION (inherited, non-blocking):** the stale `--keep-recent` /
  `--keep-recent 3` text in `proxy/README.md` is deliberately left unfixed here
  (out of scope; candidate follow-up item).

Retire the deprecated `local-only` wire value with a **loud** `400` (parent AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4): never a silent demotion to `local-preferred` and never a silent resolution to the default. This child also builds the retirement mechanism that the later `prefer-local` retirement reuses, so the two retirements share exactly one implementation.

## Goal

A client still sending `local-only` gets an attributable, actionable failure instead of a policy it did not ask for (silent demotion to a local-first default could bill a cost-capped client - the LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG lesson).

## Scope

- Remove the `local-only` entry from `LEGACY_PREFERENCE_ALIASES` (and delete the alias table if nothing remains in it) and drop `PREF_LOCAL_ONLY` from the live vocabulary.
- Extend the **single** parse/validation site (`admission_reserve.parse_preference()`) with a retired-value outcome carrying the retired value and its successor guidance; no second parser and no per-call-site comparison.
- Emit the `400` at the request entry point **before** any routing, queueing, lease, dispatch or cooldown state is written; the body is stable (`error`, `code: local_preference_retired`, `detail` naming `local-preferred` as the successor and pointing a zero-remote-spend client at a local-only *chain*).
- Exactly one `WARNING` per rejection, carrying the retired value, the successor guidance and the session id when present.
- Scope guard (parent AC3): provider names, the refusal log prefix `local_only_refused`, the internal builders and the `local_only_no_local_route` reason token stay unchanged.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

Bound `local-preferred` deferral at **three** consecutive retryable local-capacity refusals, then let the request fall back to remote instead of emitting a fourth `429` (parent AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC10). Reuses the existing retryability decision and the existing promotion shape - no third promotion path and no second classification.

## Goal

An unattended `local-preferred` worker currently spins on retryable `429`s for as long as the GPU stays contended (the 2026-10-25 incident shape). After three refusals it must get an answer from a paid tier, visibly, rather than nothing.

## Scope

- New bounded, TTL'd, per-session counter store (`proxy/proxy/local_deferral.py`, or an equivalent small dedicated module) keyed by the sanitised `X-Session-ID`; no unbounded growth, entry cap + TTL.
- Increment where `_refusal_retry_timing()` already decides retryability; the counter never re-classifies a refusal.
- At the threshold, strip the local entry for that request using `_promote_too_large_local_request()`'s shape and stamp `X-Local-Route: remote` + the new canonical token `deferral_refusals_exhausted` (registered in `LOCAL_FALLBACK_REASON_TOKENS`).
- Additive refusal-body fields `deferral_refusals` and `deferral_refusals_remaining` (0 on the third refusal), with every pre-existing field and header unchanged.
- Exactly one log line per escalation naming the session, the refusal count and the threshold.
- New config key `local_deferral_max_refusals` (default `3`, `0` disables) documented in `proxy/config.yaml` with the existing server-restart convention.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/local_deferral.py` (new module for the bounded counter store)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/proxy/session.py`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_deferral_budget.py` (new, created by the contract-test child)

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (bounded budget, parent AC5).** Refusals 1, 2 and 3 are unchanged in timing and shape (`retryable: true`, `Retry-After`/`retry_at`, `X-Local-Route: refused`); the fourth request from the same session is **not** refused - the local entry is dropped for that request and the remote tier serves it.
- **AC2 (visible, never silent, parent AC6).** The escalation returns the upstream status with `X-Local-Route: remote` and `X-Local-Fallback-Reason: deferral_refusals_exhausted`; exactly one log line names the session, count and threshold; the escalation is distinguishable from a `too_large` promotion in both header and log; no `Retry-After` is advertised on the terminal path.
- **AC3 (the refusal advertises its budget, parent AC7).** The body reports `deferral_refusals` (count so far) and `deferral_refusals_remaining` (0 on the third), purely additive - pre-existing fields, headers and key order unchanged.
- **AC4 (lifecycle and bounded memory, parent AC8).** The counter resets on a successful local dispatch, on a non-retryable refusal or `too_large` promotion, on TTL expiry, and on `local_deferral_max_refusals` reconfiguration; the store is capped and TTL'd; a request with no resolvable session id keeps today's unbounded behaviour. One test per reset trigger.
- **AC5 (one knob, parent AC10).** `local_deferral_max_refusals` is the only threshold source (default `3`); `0` restores unbounded deferral; documented as restart-required; no other default changes.
- **AC6 (no queue/lease leak, parent Constraints).** An escalated request never first enqueues and then dispatches remotely - the escalation decision is made before queue entry (or the entry is released), asserted with the fake transport.
- **AC7 (cost-capped escape hatch, parent AC9).** A remote-less chain (`private`) keeps refusing after the third refusal instead of escalating; the pin-local predicate and its five call sites agree on the escalation decision.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add the counter store with TTL, cap and a reset API; unit-test it directly.
2. Hook the increment into the single retryability decision and the reset into the local-success / `too_large` / non-retryable paths.
3. Reuse the `too_large` promotion shape for the escalation and register the token in the single token table.
4. Add the two body fields in the single refusal builder and the escalation log line.
5. Add the config key and its commentary, then fill in the deferral-budget specs.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the contract-test child. Independent of the vocabulary children (do not rebase its counter onto a preference comparison - use the existing pin predicate).

# Annotate the post-cancel release lag so a draining slot is never reported saturated

Close the last 12 `saturated`-without-live-work polls by making the proxy
annotate the slot it is still draining: every abandonment records a matchable
identity (or an endpoint-wide entry), so a draining slot reads
`abandoned_busy` and only genuinely live work reports `saturated`.

## Problem statement

The AC1 fix (`LP-0MVT2KSN3007QYFK`) took `capacity_hint=saturated` with
`local_in_flight_requests=0` and `slots_detail_stale=false` from **247 polls
(2.12 %)** to **12 polls (0.11 %)** over a comparable 11 h night, but not to
zero. Every remaining violation is a *draining* slot: llama-server has been
told to stop (the upstream stream was closed) yet has not freed the slot, and
nothing annotates it — `local_abandoned_slots=0`, so the poll reads
`saturated` even though nothing the proxy is waiting for occupies the pool.

The gap is therefore an **annotation** gap, not a liveness gap: the proxy
knows it abandoned the work, but the status builder cannot tie that
abandonment to the slot the backend is still draining.

## Users

- **Proxy operator / on-call.** Reads `/llama/local/status` to decide whether
  the machine is genuinely busy. A `saturated` hint from a draining ghost
  misdirects triage and hides real saturation (alarm fatigue).
- **Routing policy / dispatchers** (including the herdr downtime worker).
  `saturated` steers work to cloud/remote providers; a ghost-driven
  `saturated` causes avoidable paid fallback.
- **Measurement analyst** re-running `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`.
  Needs every residual poll attributable, otherwise the next re-measurement is
  as unexplained as this one.

User stories:

- As an on-call operator, when the pool holds only work the proxy abandoned, I
  want `capacity_hint=abandoned_busy` (not `saturated`) so I can tell "busy
  because of us" from "busy because of live work".
- As the routing policy, I want a draining slot to never look saturated, so a
  needless cloud fallback is not triggered by work nobody is waiting for.
- As an analyst, I want each draining-slot abandonment attributable to a slot
  or to its endpoint, so a re-measured residual can be explained rather than
  merely counted.

## Evidence (from the AC4 run, preserved)

Re-measurement `LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037`, night 2026-10-29 20:00 → 2026-10-30
07:00, artifacts in `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-29_night-post-deploy/`
(`saturated_without_live_work_attribution.csv`, 12 rows, all fresh detail):

| episode | polls | attribution | gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-30 06:57:36 | 3 (one second) | unattributable | `measured_cache_deficit` release 31 s earlier; `available_slots=0 total_slots=2 local_abandoned_slots=0`; pool idle again by 06:57:43 |
| 2026-10-30 06:01:20–21 | 2 | unattributable | — |
| 2026-10-29 20:19:25 | 1 | `session_evicted` | 295 s |
| 2026-10-29 20:35:03 | 1 | `prefill_deadline` | 14 s |
| 2026-10-29 23:36:23 | 2 | `no_progress_watchdog` | 182 s |
| 2026-10-29 23:47:30–31 | 2 | `prefill_deadline` | 48 s |
| 2026-10-30 01:43:11 | 1 | `session_evicted` | 520 s |

Two shapes of the same gap:

1. **Attributable (7 polls)** — an abandonment whose cancel succeeded leaves a
   slot that is still `is_processing` but carries **no** abandoned-registry
   entry (`local_abandoned_slots=0`), so the annotation does not fire.
2. **Unattributable (5 polls)** — a release with no slot identity at all
   (`measured_cache_deficit` on a record without a pinned slot), so the poll
   cannot be attributed even with the 600 s lookback.

Two further observations to confirm during implementation (not yet claimed as
causes):

- two rows (06:01:20, 01:43:11) report `available_slots=1` **alongside**
  `saturated`, which a purely-occupied pool cannot produce;
- one row reports `latency_ms=3355`, above the `/slots` detail budget, while
  `slots_detail_stale=false`.

If either turns out to be a distinct (non-lag) defect, record it as a
`discovered-from:LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM` item rather than widening this one.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every abandonment path records a registry entry that can match the slot it
   gave up on, or records an explicit "unknown slot, endpoint-wide" entry that
   the status builder can match to a processing slot on that endpoint (so a
   release without a slot id is still annotatable).
2. A drained-but-still-`is_processing` slot is annotated `abandoned_busy`
   until llama-server reports it free (registry TTL keeps it bounded; no
   leaked marker, no double decrement, no phantom lease).
3. `capacity_hint` for that state stays `abandoned_busy`, never `saturated`
   and never `idle`; a genuinely live, proxy-owned slot still reports
   `saturated` (the truthful-status contract of `LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM` is not
   weakened).
4. Deterministic tests (mocked `/slots` snapshot, injected clock) cover both
   shapes above, including the case where the draining slot is visible in a
   *fresh* snapshot, the endpoint-wide (unknown-slot) match, and the negative
   case (endpoint-wide entry present but the slot is owned by a live dispatch
   record → still `saturated`).
5. Re-measurement over a comparable night shows **0** `saturated`-without-live-
   work polls (baseline for this residual: 12 polls / 0.11 %, of which 5
   unattributable).
6. Full suite green through the `test` skill; docs updated where the
   abandonment → capacity interaction is described
   (`proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`).
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Truthful status is not weakened** (`LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM`): an endpoint-wide
  match must never annotate a slot that a live dispatch record owns, and a
  fresh snapshot with genuinely live decode work must keep reporting
  `saturated`.
- The registry stays **in-process**, keyed by `(endpoint, slot)`, lazily
  pruned, TTL-bounded (`DEFAULT_ABANDONED_SLOT_TTL_SECONDS`, 900 s default), no
  timer task, no unbounded growth. An endpoint-wide entry needs a key that
  cannot collide with a real slot id.
- The annotation is **read-only status decoration**: it must never free or
  acquire capacity, double-decrement counters, or create a phantom lease.
- The status schema stays **additive** (`status_schema_version` 4:
  `abandoned*`, `local_abandoned_slots`, `capacity_hint=abandoned_busy`).
- **Measurement must remain possible.** `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`
  `_ABANDON_REASONS` currently excludes `measured_cache_deficit`, so that
  release is reported unattributable no matter how well the proxy annotates
  it — the set must be extended (with a test) or AC5 is unmeasurable.
- Agent test runs go through `/skill:test` only; no ad-hoc `pytest`.

## Existing state

- Registry: `_abandoned_slots` (`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`), keyed
  `(endpoint_or_empty, slot_id)`; `_record_abandoned_slot` returns `None` when
  the slot id is not an `int`, so an unknown-slot abandonment is silently
  dropped — this is exactly the shape-2 gap.
- Matching: `_abandoned_slot_for(slot_id, endpoint=…)` tries the exact
  endpoint, then the legacy/default endpoint, then any endpoint carrying that
  slot id. There is no endpoint-wide (slot-less) match.
- Recording paths: `_release_unserved_dispatch` resolves the slot via
  `_abandoned_slot_lookup` *before* freeing the assignment (prefill deadline,
  client disconnect); session eviction resolves one slot per released record
  in `proxy/proxy/server.py`; the watchdog and orphan sweep record too.
  `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch` passes **neither** slot id nor
  stream, which is the shape-2 source.
- Status builder: `proxy/proxy/observability.py` annotates `abandoned`,
  `abandonment_reason`, `abandoned_session_id`, `abandoned_at_seconds_ago`
  when the registry matches the slot id; `compute_capacity_hint` rule 0
  returns `abandoned_busy` when every generating slot is abandoned and keeps
  `saturated` when any generating slot is live.
- Residual behaviour: the 7 attributable polls reported
  `local_abandoned_slots=0` while a slot was `is_processing`, so the recorded
  identity did not match the draining slot (stale/mis-resolved id, or a slot
  the backend reassigned after the free) and the annotation never fired.
- Docs already describe the mechanism in
  `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md` (§ *Abandoned work*) and
  `proxy/docs/routing.md` (§ *Abandoned local dispatches*).

## Desired change

1. Every abandonment path records either the slot it gave up on (resolved
   before the assignment is freed, and re-verified against the slot the
   backend actually reports) or an explicit endpoint-wide "unknown slot" entry.
2. The status builder matches an endpoint-wide entry only to a processing slot
   on that endpoint that no live dispatch record owns, so the draining ghost is
   annotated and live work is not.
3. The annotation survives until llama-server reports the slot free (or the TTL
   elapses), and is dropped when the slot is observed free; re-abandoning
   refreshes it; no duplicate entries, no leak.
4. `capacity_hint` for a pool whose only work is draining stays
   `abandoned_busy` — never `saturated`, never `idle`.
5. `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` counts a `measured_cache_deficit`
   release as an abandonment event for attribution, with a test.
6. Docs updated where the abandonment → capacity interaction is described.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — abandoned-slot registry, release paths,
  endpoint-wide entry, slot re-verification.
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — status slot builder, endpoint-wide match,
  `compute_capacity_hint` (rule 0 unchanged in intent).
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `/llama/local/status` payload
  (`local_abandoned_slots`).
- `proxy/proxy/server.py` — session-eviction slot resolution (if the recorded
  identity needs re-verification).
- `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py` — registry, annotation and
  capacity-hint tests for both shapes.
- `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py` — status payload contract.
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_capacity_signal_verification.py` — attribution set.
- `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md` — docs.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the 7 attributable residuals are identity/matching failures,
  not TTL expiry — the longest release→poll gap observed is 520 s against a
  900 s TTL. Verify by logging the recorded slot id against the processing slot
  id during implementation.
- **Assumption:** AC5 (night re-measurement) is an operational run after
  deploy, mirroring the parent's child `LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037`; the plan step may
  decompose it into a follow-on child instead of blocking the code change.
- **Risk:** an endpoint-wide match annotates live work → weakens the truthful
  contract. Mitigation: require no live dispatch record for that slot, and
  cover the negative case with a deterministic test (AC4).
- **Risk:** a slot reported free and immediately reassigned could inherit a
  stale endpoint-wide entry. Mitigation: clear the entry on an observed free
  slot and keep the bounded TTL.
- **Risk (scope creep):** cooldown behaviour (`prefill_thrash_cooldown`) and
  the two anomalous rows (`available_slots=1`, 3.3 s latency) are **out of
  scope** here; record them as `discovered-from` items if confirmed.
- **Risk:** extending `_ABANDON_REASONS` changes the historical baseline
  (247 / 12 poll counts were computed with the narrower set). Mitigation: state
  the change in the report note and in the docs.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB` — parent: abandoned local dispatches leave
  llama-server busy (completed).
- `LP-0MVT2KSN3007QYFK` — AC1: abandoned-slot registry and upstream cancel
  (completed; this item closes its residual).
- `LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037` — AC4: re-measure one comparable night (completed;
  produced the 12-poll baseline).
- `LP-0MVT2KS1R006P8E2` — regression test: abandoned dispatch not reported
  saturated (completed).
- `LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM` — truthful-status contract (stale capacity hint
  reconciliation) that this item must not weaken.
- `LP-0MVT2KWF0000QTSM` — docs for abandoned-work status and cooldown scope
  (completed).
- Docs: `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`,
  `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/README.md`; artifacts under
  `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-29_night-post-deploy/`.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is a producer interview needed before drafting, or does the seed context
  suffice?" — Answer (agent, from repo/worklog evidence): the seed context
  states the problem, the measured evidence, the target outcome, six testable
  ACs and the key files; no producer input is required to draft. Source:
  `wl show LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM` (description authored by Map), evidence CSV in
  `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-29_night-post-deploy/`.
- Q: "Does AC5 (night re-measurement) block the code change?" — Answer (agent,
  precedent): the parent split re-measurement into its own child
  (`LP-0MVT2KW5A008X037`), so the plan step should decompose AC5 the same way.
  **Open to producer override**, not blocking; recorded as an assumption above.
- Q: "Is `measured_cache_deficit` outside the abandonment reasons the
  verification script attributes?" — Answer (agent, code evidence): yes —
  `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` `_ABANDON_REASONS` lists only
  `prefill_deadline`, `session_evicted`, `no_progress_watchdog`,
  `client_disconnect`, while `proxy/proxy/measured_cache_abort.py` exports
  `MEASURED_CACHE_DEFICIT_REASON`. Captured as constraint 5 / AC-relevant scope.
- Q: "Why did the 7 attributable polls still show
  `local_abandoned_slots=0`?" — Answer (OPEN QUESTION, for implementation):
  not determinable from the artifacts alone (no recorded-slot-id field in the
  12-row CSV). Recorded as an assumption to verify with logging, not resolved
  at intake.
### Plan-stage Q&A (added by /skill:plan, session herdr-1793358530-3252013-3553)

- Q: "Is an endpoint-wide (slot-less) registry entry safe, or does it risk
  annotating live work and weakening the truthful contract?" — Answer (agent,
  code evidence + design): safe when the matcher requires that the processing
  slot has **no** lease owner and no live dispatch record; the negative case is
  pinned by a deterministic test before implementation
  (`LP-0MVUVHA55009EU4B`), and `compute_capacity_hint` rule 0 is unchanged in
  intent (`proxy/proxy/observability.py`). Source: `annotate_slots_for_status`
  already computes `owner_session_id`; `_build_slot_to_session_map` provides the
  dispatch-record binding.
- Q: "Should an endpoint-wide entry annotate a slot read from a *stale*
  `/slots` snapshot, and should a stale snapshot clear the entry?" — Answer
  (agent, design decision): annotate yes, clear **no**. The registry entry is
  fresh evidence about an abandonment, while `is_processing=false` is only
  trustworthy from a fresh snapshot; clearing on stale detail would let a
  cached "free" reading drop a live annotation, and the stale path is already
  reconciled by `downgrade_stale_capacity_hint` (LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM).
- Q: "Which key can represent 'endpoint-wide' without colliding with a real

  sentinel would break the type contract. Recorded as a module constant so the

- Q: "Why did the 7 attributable polls still show `local_abandoned_slots=0`?"
  — **OPEN QUESTION (carried forward, not resolved at plan time)**: not

- Q: "Does AC5 (night re-measurement) block the code change?" — Answer (agent,

# Goal

Author the **red-first** test suite that encodes the new `/slots` read-path contract *before* any
implementation, so every implementation child in this plan is driven by failing tests rather than
written first and tested afterwards.

These tests pin the behaviour that makes `slots_stale` measurable and small: one bounded upstream
fetch per refresh cycle, a snapshot-age freshness definition, and untouched reconciliation
guarantees for `capacity_hint`.

# Test matrix

1. **Fan-out.** N concurrent `GET /llama/local/status` polls inside the freshness window issue
   **exactly one** upstream `/slots` request. Extend the existing coalescing suite rather than
   writing a second harness.
2. **Latency bound.** With an injected backend that never answers, the status handler returns
   within the configured budget (`STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT`) plus a small slack — it must not serialise
   counts (2 s) + detail (1 s) + status (1 s) awaits.
3. **Age-derived freshness.** A table-driven test asserts `slots_stale` follows the published
   snapshot age versus the freshness budget: `age < budget ⇒ false`, `age == budget ⇒ false`,
   `age > budget ⇒ true`, and `missing snapshot ⇒ true`.
4. **Additive schema.** A consumer that ignores unknown fields sees unchanged `available_slots` /
   `total_slots` / `slots` semantics; the payload carries the versioned schema field.
5. **Stale reconciliation unchanged.** For every stale-snapshot fixture, `capacity_hint` is never
   `saturated` while `local_in_flight_requests == 0` (LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM AC3 must survive this

## Goal

Make every proxy release of an accepted local dispatch **attributable to a
backend task lifecycle**, and correct the abandoned-prefill window model, so
"prefills computed and thrown away" is a measurement rather than the
subtraction of two counters.

Parent: LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2 — AC2 (the instrument), with the model correction
AC1 needs and AC5's docstring requirement.

## Target outcome

`proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` (or a sibling module it
imports) joins `local_eviction_after_acceptance` / `lease_released` events to
`llama-server.log` task lifecycles over a ≥24 h restart-segmented window and
reports: releases with no explained backend stop (count + share), the
cancel→`stop processing` latency distribution, tokens evaluated after the
cancel, and unjoined releases. The abandoned-prefill windows are derived from
observed stops, with the legacy token/rate basis retained for comparability.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Release→cancel accounting exists and is produced from on-disk logs
  only.** A function (e.g. `release_cancel_accounting(...)`) emits, per
  window: `releases_total`, `releases_with_observed_cancel`,
  `releases_without_explained_backend_stop` (count and share),
  `releases_unjoined` (count and per-event reason), `cancel_to_stop_seconds`
  p10/p50/p90, and `tokens_evaluated_after_cancel` (totals and per-event).
- **AC2 — CLI exposure.** The script gains a documented way to point at the
  `llama-server` log(s) for a window (reusing/extending `--llama-log`) and
  emits the accounting in the JSON dataset; `--json` output stays
  machine-parseable and the text summary states the accounting headline.
- **AC3 — Nothing is dropped.** Every release appears exactly once: joined,
  unjoined-with-reason, or explained-by-another-mechanism. The sums are
  asserted by the sibling test item.
- **AC4 — Window model corrected, both bases kept.** `abandoned_prefill_windows()`
  derives each window's end from the observed backend stop when one exists and
  marks the row `bounded=true/false`; `ABANDONED_PREFILL_RATE_TOK_S` remains
  available as the legacy basis, and the report carries both the legacy and
  corrected overlap counts for `prefill_deadline` events (so 58/60 can be
  restated on both bases).
- **AC5 — Docstring tells the truth.** `abandoned_prefill_windows()`'s
  docstring no longer asserts "a released dispatch is **not** cancelled at
  `llama-server`"; it states what is measured, what is estimated, and the
  provenance of each constant.
- **AC6 — Tests from both test-first items pass**; `proxy/tests/test_prefill_deadline_residual_analysis.py`
  keeps passing unchanged; the full suite is green through `/skill:test`.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Parse `llama-server.log` lines into task-lifecycle records: `launch_slot_`
  (slot/task), `update_slots … prompt processing progress` (`n_tokens`,
  `batch.n_tokens`, `progress`), `srv stop: cancel task, id_task = N`,
  `slot release: … stop processing`, `prompt eval time`.
2. Join each release to a task by (a) `llama_task_id`/`slot_id` when the log
   line carries them, else (b) the session's slot at release + nearest
   preceding `launch_slot_` for that slot; record how each join was made and
   count the unjoined residue.
3. Emit the accounting block in `build_report()` and the text summary.
4. Re-point `abandoned_prefill_windows()` at observed stops, keeping the
   legacy estimate under an explicit `bounded=false` label, and have
   `backlog_evidence()`/`attribute_events()` report both bases.
5. Rewrite the `abandoned_prefill_windows()` docstring per AC5.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` — the analyser
  (`abandoned_prefill_windows()`, `backlog_evidence()`, `build_report()`,
  `backend_prefill_accounting()`, `parse_args()`, `_text_summary()`).
- `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_prefill_release_cancel.py` — joiner tests.
- `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_prefill_windows_measured.py` — window-model tests.
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_deadline_residual_analysis.py` — must stay green.
- `proxy/tests/fixtures/` — the fixture pair from the test-first item.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the two test-first items (joiner contract, window-model contract).

## Constraints

- Log-only measurement (no in-process counters), per
  `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md`.
- `llama-server.log` lines carry no wall-clock timestamp: the joiner must be
  valid only for a file that covers the analysed window, and must say so when
  it cannot establish coverage (same caveat as
  `backend_prefill_accounting()`).
- Do not change the *definition* of `EVICTION_REASONS_AFTER_ACCEPTANCE` or the
  eviction log line format here (that is the routing item's business).
